newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian c.bank okays Vereins Bank permit.
newsitem.headline: Latvian c.bank okays Vereins Bank permit.

text.p: Latvia's central bank said that it has given a licence to German Vereins und Westbank, part of the Vereins Bank group, to open a branch in the Latvian capital.

The central bank said in a statement released late on Thursday that the new bank would have share capital of 3.9 million lats and would work as a universal bank with its main field of activity in the finance of foreign trade.

"This is real proof that international trust in Latvia and its economy is growing, that the bank crisis has been overcome and that the reforms to create stability in the bank system are being carried out successfully," the central bank said.
Latvia last year suffered one of eastern Europe's worst bank crises when its largest bank was shut by the regulators.
The closure and the folding of other banks resulted in an economic slowdown and played havoc with state finances.
With the Vereins Bank branch, Latvia now has two foreign banks on its territory as Societe Generale opened here in 1995.
The central bank said the German bank branch would aim to service clients in Latvia, the other Baltic states, Germany and Scandinavia.
